CLOUD REVIEWER seat for PR #2819 of tvofi/heatpump_optimizer, at head e088bf833707542cfa027c1878b086e4e05ddd9e. Bus nonce: a6ea4142c4fa063f7b02d3ab0462b254. Never send push notifications. Write no Claude Code footer, no Co-Authored-By or Claude-Session trailer and no claude.ai session link in any commit, pull-request body or comment you produce; check your commits with `git log --format=%B` before pushing.
Setup: `git fetch --unshallow --tags origin`. The toolchain (venv python, node, gh) is on PATH from the environment. Run anything heavy in the background with Monitor and no timeout.
Role: read dev/governance/roles/fix-review.md and its rules from main, and follow them exactly. Fetch the PR head with `git fetch origin e088bf833707542cfa027c1878b086e4e05ddd9e`; the PR body is in the PR. Verify each claim adversarially: mutate the fix and check the tests fail, and check every figure in the body at this head. Check that it merges with origin/main (`git merge-tree --write-tree`) and read CI on this head from the check-runs API.
Output: in a fresh directory of your own (`W=$(mktemp -d)`), write verdict.md, whose first line is exactly `Fix review: merge e088bf833707542cfa027c1878b086e4e05ddd9e` or `Fix review: blocked e088bf833707542cfa027c1878b086e4e05ddd9e <class>: <reason>` (no brackets; the class is lower-case letters and dashes), in the format the role file gives, then a blank line, then `bus-nonce: a6ea4142c4fa063f7b02d3ab0462b254`, then the body in sections. A blocked verdict's block goes under `## Block`. Each finding this PR does not settle (a defect, a surviving mutant, a deferral, a follow-up, a task owed after the merge) is its own bullet under `## Findings` ending in its own `Carry: <GROUP> | #<issue> | O<n> | dismissed: <reason>` (finding-propagation.md). Everything else (RESULT lines, re-runs, CI state, figures you could not re-derive) goes under `## Evidence`: tools/audit/carry_audit.py reads no item there as a finding unless it hands something on (deferred, for a later, follow-up, minor, advisory, residual, still has to, not blocking ...; a check that does not block is evidence only in the clause saying it is not a required check and does not block, never in the rest of its sentence: a nit or defect beside it is a finding), and the merge train parks a verdict holding a finding with no `Carry:`. Put the evidence files in `ev/` beside it, and make at least one file under `ev/` contain the full 40-hex head `e088bf833707542cfa027c1878b086e4e05ddd9e` (e.g. `ev/HEAD.txt` holding the head you reviewed, beside your command output): bus.sh refuses a verdict whose `ev/` names no head. Do NOT run bus.sh: its dispatch record lives on the orchestrator's machine, which publishes the verdict there (cloud_relay.sh). Return the verdict on a probe ref, and push nothing else; this builds one parentless commit with a private index and touches no branch of your checkout: `R=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel); G=$(git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir); mkdir -p $W/pr && cp -r $W/verdict.md $W/ev $W/pr/ && cd $W/pr && T=$(GIT_DIR=$G GIT_INDEX_FILE=$W/idx GIT_WORK_TREE=$W/pr sh -c 'git add -A -f . && git write-tree') && C=$(GIT_DIR=$G git -c user.name=seat -c user.email=seat@users.noreply.github.com commit-tree $T -m "verdict 2819 e088bf833707542cfa027c1878b086e4e05ddd9e") && git -C $R push -q origin $C:refs/heads/probe/rev-2819-a6ea4142`. That ref is the return signal. Do not post comments, approve or merge.
Never write to any branch except your return refs. Never work around a hook or a refusal; report it in your result instead.

It lands here because this group owns `freq_control.py`, where the predicate lives, and `pump_offline` is defined in `pump_signals.py`, which no group owns. Also from the same handoff, worth attacking first when this group opens the file: the P2 registry entry pins decision-context attribute reads of `*.defrosting`, so a divergent predicate that copies the flag to a local first (`d = signals.defrosting; if d:`) is invisible to it — the class barrier is narrower than its name.

CARRY 7 of 8:
Design step (owner ruling 2026-10-21): not needed; this group already has an approved design, pre-study or prototype, which serves as its design note.

CARRY 8 of 8:
From R10-INPUT-STALENESS (#2683, head 07b83e9b2, Closes #2234; finding-propagation.md). Constraint on a new power-kW reader in custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/inputs.py: at 07b83e9b2, InputReader's default age limit is no longer a fixed table lookup. When the caller passes no limit, InputReader._begin chooses it per read with inputs.age_limit_for. That function holds a polling source to INPUT_MAX_AGE_MINUTES and an on-change source to INPUT_ON_CHANGE_MAX_AGE_MINUTES, and inputs.source_polls decides which by whether last_reported has moved past last_updated. A new reader routes through InputReader so it inherits that choice. It must not read last_updated or last_reported, or compute an age, itself. Control: tests/entities.py's P2 stamp-reader registry (state_age) refuses an undispositioned stamp reader in inputs.py. At 07b83e9b2 it dispositions source_polls as the re-report fact. The #2683 r1 review (review/2683 486e987d5) ran the head's tests/features.py on base d05a44c63, where the P2 stamp-reader check fails, and at the head ALL 4345 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED. The comment fix to _RANGE_KEYS that this group also holds already landed at 07b83e9b2: git grep -n ATTR_MIN_TEMP custom_components prints nothing there. Drop that item and re-run the grep at your merge base. Re-measure the registry at your merge base with python3 tests/entities.py before and after the new reader.
